@@ -534,6 +534,18 @@ cx doctor fix-overlaps --config cx.toml --interactive
 
 Interactive mode is the safest choice when the recommended owner is not obviously correct.
 
+If you want dynamic overlap resolution without implicit tie-break ownership,
+use:
+
+```toml
+[dedup]
+mode = "first-wins"
+require_explicit_ownership = true
+```
+
+That keeps the dynamic ownership model, but turns equal-priority overlaps back
+into hard failures instead of silently falling back to config or lexical order.
+

files.patch:
@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420122000
 title: Bundle Index Rename To Shared Handover
 tags: ["handover", "naming", "architecture"]
-target: v0.4
+target: current
 ---
 The current term "bundle index" is now too narrow because the file already acts as a shared handover artifact for both humans and agents, not just a lookup-oriented section listing.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420124000
 title: Contract Versioning Strategy
 tags: ["contracts", "versioning", "governance"]
-target: v0.4
+target: current
 ---
 Contract surfaces need explicit versioning when `cx` chooses hard breaks over deprecation layers.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420121500
 title: Extension Config Model
 tags: ["config", "plugins", "schema"]
-target: v0.4
+target: backlog
 ---
 Extensions must declare explicit configuration so plugin settings can remain bounded, schema-visible, and incapable of silently mutating kernel behavior.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420120400
 title: Internal API Stabilization
 tags: ["architecture", "api", "refactor"]
-target: v0.4
+target: backlog
 ---
 The system must stabilize internal interfaces before adding plugins.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420110800
 title: Kernel vs Extension Boundary
 tags: ["architecture", "boundary", "plugins"]
-target: v0.4
+target: current
 ---
 The system enforces a strict separation between kernel and extensions.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420121000
 title: Native Render Migration Strategy
 tags: ["migration", "render", "repomix"]
-target: v0.4
+target: current
 ---
 The render engine must transition from Repomix to a native kernel without changing proof behavior, because migration is only safe when the proof path stays identical while ownership moves inward. XML, Markdown, Plain, JSON, and the shared handover now run through kernel-owned paths, native structured-plan construction now belongs to the kernel, adapter-plan extraction exists only for parity comparison, and the Repomix path is now parity-only rather than a hidden runtime fallback; the remaining work is shrinking the oracle boundary until it no longer defines the runtime proof path at all.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420130200
 title: Notes Gating Policy
 tags: ["notes", "governance", "quality"]
-target: v0.4
+target: backlog
 ---
 Notes may act as optional build constraints in higher-assurance environments.

 id: 20260420130000
 title: Overlap Strict Mode
 tags: ["bundle", "determinism", "sections"]

+target: current
 ---
 Overlap resolution must be explicit in strict environments.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420120300
 title: Plugin Capability Tiers
 tags: ["plugins", "security", "architecture"]
-target: v0.4
+target: backlog
 ---
 Plugins are classified by trust and capability.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420121100
 title: Plugin Lifecycle Policy
 tags: ["plugins", "governance", "lifecycle"]
-target: v0.4
+target: backlog
 ---
 Plugins follow a strict lifecycle so extension systems stay governable even when new capabilities arrive quickly.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 id: 20260420110200
 title: Plugin System Model
 tags: ["architecture", "plugins", "extensibility"]
-target: v0.4
+target: backlog

 `cx` introduces a bounded plugin system layered on top of the kernel.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@

 tags: ["release", "assurance", "proof"]
-target: v0.4
+target: current
 ---
 A release is valid only if proof invariants hold, because release success is not just green CI but continued evidence that rendering, manifests, extraction, and verification still mean the same thing.

 The render kernel defines the proof-path behavior of `cx`.

 `security_check` evolves into a pluggable scanner pipeline.

 id: 20260420120500
 title: Scanner Pipeline Contract
 tags: ["security", "scanner"]
-target: v0.4
+target: backlog
 ---
 Security scanning is a pluggable pipeline, not a renderer feature.

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@

+target: current
 ---
 The shared handover must not increase generated file count casually because bundle comprehension, verification, and extraction all become more expensive when context is split across too many generated companion files.
